blocks.content: By noon, Ethan had set up his small travel easel near the edge of the park.
He had not followed her there.
That was important. He told himself that three times.

The light was good. The archway had a nice shape. The fountain was broken in an interesting way. Those were all legitimate artistic reasons that had nothing to do with the fact that he chose the bench near the archway as the center of the composition.
He squeezed out blue, white, green. Worked the first layer loose — sky, trees, stone, water. He kept his headphones in with nothing playing, the universal signal for please do not perceive me.
It mostly worked.
Until a voice behind him said:

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: That fountain looks better in your painting than it does in real life.
Ethan startled so hard he nearly dragged a line of blue across the canvas.
He turned.
Red hair. Green jacket. Purple dinosaur. Her.
His brain, normally unreliable in social settings, decided this was the perfect moment to resign completely.

blocks.speaker: Ethan
blocks.content: Uh.
Excellent. A strong opening.

Up close she was striking in a way that had nothing to do with looking polished. Small freckle near one cheekbone. A smudge of ink on one finger. Wind had pulled loose strands of hair across her face, and she had zero interest in fixing them.
She looks real. Somehow that makes it worse.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: I didn't mean to scare you.

blocks.speaker: Ethan
blocks.content: You didn't.
His voice came out too fast. She glanced at the brush, then at the tiny blue mark now streaked across his knuckle.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: You sure?

blocks.speaker: Ethan
blocks.content: Oh.
She smiled. There it was again. The thrown match.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: I'm Cassandra.
Ethan stared for half a second too long before remembering names were usually exchanged in these situations.

blocks.speaker: Ethan
blocks.content: Ethan.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: Ethan the painter.

blocks.speaker: Ethan
blocks.content: I guess.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: You guess?

blocks.speaker: Ethan
blocks.content: I mean, yes. Technically.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: Technically a painter?

blocks.speaker: Ethan
blocks.content: That sounded less dumb in my head.
